unit.title: Parts of the soul II
unit.needIt: Understanding how your brain works helps you see why you make quick mistakes or feel sudden urges. It helps you realize that your first instinct isn't always your best choice.
unit.why: Our brains have two systems. One is fast and automatic, like a reflex. The other is slow and logical, like solving a math problem. Sometimes, these two systems fight each other, leading us to make choices that don't make sense.
unit.outcome: Identify when your automatic habits are overriding your logical goals.

quiz.why: The lecture explains that using a non-representative group leads to inaccurate information.
quiz.quote: We used a measure which doesn't give us accurate information about what we wanted to find out.

quiz.why: The lecture defines WEIRD as a specific group of people often used in psychological research.
quiz.quote: And weird here stands for Western, educated, industrialized, rich, and democratic.

quiz.q: Why did people find the question about 'b1 plus b2' harder than 'x plus y'?
choices: They did not know the letters
It was a different type of math
quiz.why: The lecture explains that using complex characters instead of simple ones lowers performance even if the math is the same.
quiz.quote: Presenting people with problems that were formally identical, but which differed in terms of the complexity of the characters used to represent them, produced a massive decrement in performance.

quiz.q: How did people react to the 'unbelievable' syllogism?
quiz.why: People struggle to see logic when the conclusion feels impossible.
quiz.quote: But as a result of the conclusion being implausible, only 55% of people were able to recognize that the conclusion followed from the premises.

quiz.q: What is the difference between a 'descriptive' rule and a 'normative' rule?
choices: Descriptive is how things are, normative is how they ought to be
Descriptive is about math, normative is about feelings
Descriptive is fast, normative is slow
quiz.why: The lecture uses these terms to explain why social rules trigger different reasoning processes.
quiz.quote: And the second difference between the bottom and the top is, of course, that this is a normative rule. It's about how things ought to be. Whereas this is a descriptive rule. It's about how things are.

quiz.q: What is a main characteristic of System 1?
quiz.why: System 1 is described as the fast, unconscious, and automatic part of our processing.
quiz.quote: System one operates automatically, whereas system two is consciously controlled.

choices: A bias based on how info is presented
quiz.why: The lecture shows how changing the way a choice is described changes the choice people make.
quiz.quote: Just one is framed in terms of who will live, the other in terms of who will die, and the result is almost a complete inversion of people's preferences.

crystal.key: Our brains use different systems that can conflict with our conscious goals.

decoys.why: The lecture shows System 1 can be biased by framing and aliefs.

decoys.text: Aliefs are the same as beliefs.
decoys.why: The lecture distinguishes aliefs as habitual propensities, while beliefs are what we think is true.

crystal.aha: Fast habits (System 1/Aliefs) often override slow logic (System 2/Beliefs).
